source_and_product_id: Same NP6-785-ER weekly/annual historical hub and load-zone archive, report 13061. Live 15-minute product NP6-905-CD / report 12301 is not stored.
observation_timestamp_convention: Hourly max of interval-start prices, UTC. Latest legal hour at issue t with delay d is t-(1+d).
assumed_or_documented_release_time: Assumed: 1 hour after the 15-minute interval ends (shortest of the pre-specified set {1,2,3,6}). EMIL states Chron-Weekly generation; 2011 notice says Sunday replacement of the current-year file. Neither gives minutes after interval end.
revision_vintage_status: High: weekly archive can include prices corrected before 1600 on the second business day, or later Board corrections. The on-disk file has no revision flag.
transformation_and_lag: Lags 1,12,24,48,168,720 and rolling 24/168 mean and std of the hourly max, shifted 1+d hours via clock_shift.
earliest_permitted_use: Issue t may use hour t-(k+d). Primary d=1 so latest price is t-2.
supporting_official_source: EMIL NP6-785-ER; 2011 NOTICE_SETTLEMENTS weekly Sunday run; Protocols 6.3(7) finality 1600 second Business Day. 2020 annual MIS DocID 751356439 contains a complete Dec 31 (96 intervals); the on-disk gap that day is the local fetch filter, not a missing ERCOT file.
remaining_uncertainty: No 2019-2024 first-publication timestamp. Applying a delay to the final archive does not reconstruct the first posted price.

observation_timestamp_convention: 15-minute Interval Start, UTC. Window is the four intervals of the last fully visible clock hour.
assumed_or_documented_release_time: Same assumed 1-hour delay after interval end.

source_and_product_id: ERCOT DAM hub SPPs. Code file is data/raw/ercot_da_prices.parquet (gridstatus DAM extract). Historical product NP4-180-ER / report 13060 (weekly). Live product NP4-190-CD / report 12331 (per DAM run).
observation_timestamp_convention: Hour start stored as UTC. On-disk DA begins 2016-01-01 06:00 UTC (= 00:00 Central) and ends 2024-12-31 06:00 UTC, the same Central-midnight fetch cut as RT.
assumed_or_documented_release_time: Documented deadline: as soon as practicable, but no later than 1330, ERCOT posts DASPPs (current Protocols 4.5.2(2), file 04-080126_Nodal.docx, access 2026-10-26). NPRR903 (posted 2018-10-02, approved 2020-08-11, effective 2020-09-01) treats the 1330 deadline as already existing and memorializes 1900 as the latest publish time after a delay. Code gate: 14:00 US/Central on D-1 for operating day D (30-minute buffer).
revision_vintage_status: DAM LMPs, MCPCs, and Settlement Point Prices are final at 1000 of the second Business Day after the Operating Day (4.5.2(6)). Board review remains possible after notice within 30 days. The file has no correction flag. A 2011 Board item still quoted finality on the next Business Day; that is not the current text.
transformation_and_lag: Publication-gated da_HB_* columns and da_shape_ramp / day_max / day_min from the gated hub series.
earliest_permitted_use: A DA hour for local operating day D is used only when issue t >= D-1 14:00 Central.
supporting_official_source: Current Protocols 4.5.2; NPRR903 issue page; EMIL NP4-180-ER and NP4-190-CD.
remaining_uncertainty: Exact historical posting minute for each 2019-2024 operating day was not re-measured. Delayed DAM runs (allowed by NPRR903) can publish after 14:00; the code would still unlock at 14:00 using the archived price.
verification_status: documented rule with uncertain historical applicability

source_and_product_id: Pipeline tries ERCOT reports 13101 (NP6-345-CD), 13100, 12311, then EIA hourly demand. On-disk file is data/raw/ercot_load.parquet. It is not a match to the Hourly Load Data Archives Native_Load workbooks.
observation_timestamp_convention: On-disk index is UTC hour-start, 24 rows on every UTC day, one NaN at 2021-11-07 06:00 UTC (fall-back hour). Native_Load 2020/2024 workbooks use Hour Ending on US/Central with HE=24 and a DST-labeled repeated hour. Official HE-as-end Central vs on-disk: 2024 MAE 1523 MW, corr 0.984. Treating the HE stamp as Central hour-start is closer (2024 MAE 275 MW, corr 0.9997; 2020 MAE 101 MW, corr 0.99994) but not exact. Naive-UTC localization of Native_Load is far worse (MAE ~7000 MW).
assumed_or_documented_release_time: NP6-345-CD: Chron-Daily, display duration 31, first run 2013-06-13; no minutes-after-hour figure. Native_Load page: previous month typically posted around the 9th. Code assumes 1 hour after the load hour ends (same pre-specified set). A 24-hour lag is a sensitivity only.
revision_vintage_status: Medium: daily or monthly archives may be revised; no revision flag. On-disk values are a different product or vintage than the Native_Load files retrieved 2026-10-26.
transformation_and_lag: load_lag_1h and load_rollmean_24h, shifted 1+d. Same-hour load is not a feature. 62.5% of crisis-fit training rows (pre-2019) have no load and are median-imputed.
earliest_permitted_use: Issue t with d=1 uses load at t-2.
supporting_official_source: EMIL NP6-345-CD; https://www.ercot.com/gridinfo/load/load_hist; alignment numbers in wp2_raw/load_alignment_variants.csv.
remaining_uncertainty: Which fetch path wrote the parquet is [MISSING]. The 1-hour-ending vs hour-starting convention is not settled against Native_Load because the series do not match. A delay applied to this file is still an assumption.

source_and_product_id: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report (WNGSR). On-disk timestamps are week-ending Fridays at 00:00 UTC.
observation_timestamp_convention: Week-ending Friday 00:00 UTC (all 851 rows have weekday=4). Report describes working gas as of the previous Friday.
assumed_or_documented_release_time: Documented standard: Thursday 10:30 a.m. Eastern. Code available_at = timestamp + 7 days 18 hours = the following Friday 18:00 UTC, after Thursday 10:30 ET and after every 2019-2024 holiday exception retrieved from Wayback (Wednesday noon ET or Friday 10:30 ET).
revision_vintage_status: Low for the timing buffer. The file can still contain later statistical revisions of the weekly stock; those are unmarked.
earliest_permitted_use: A week-ending Friday F is used only when issue t >= F + 7 days 18 hours.
supporting_official_source: Live schedule https://ir.eia.gov/ngs/schedule.html (2026-10-26, 2025-26 exceptions only); Wayback tables in wp2_raw/eia_wngsr_exceptions_2019_2024.csv; EIA Today in Energy 2023-06-22 (id=56900).
remaining_uncertainty: The code does not join on the actual release timestamp. Friday 00:00 UTC as the week-ending stamp is 6 hours before Friday 00:00 US/Eastern.
verification_status: documented rule with uncertain historical applicability

observation_timestamp_convention: US/Central civil time of issue t. Peak = weekday 16:00-22:00 Central.
